sections.title: My, your and his/her/their
sections.content: Possessive adjectives come before the noun. *Mi* means "my", *tu* means "your", and *su* means "his", "her" or "their". They have plural forms before plural nouns: *mis*, *tus*, *sus*.

items.english: His / Her / Their father is from Chile.

sections.content: The possessive agrees with the noun in number, not with the owner: *mi hermano*, *mis hermanos*.

sections.title: Introducing someone: *él es* / *ella es*
sections.content: You know *él es* and *ella es* from Unit 2. To introduce a family member, add a possessive: *Ella es mi madre*. *Él* or *ella* depends on the person you are introducing, not on you.
